title: Cabinet Refinishing in Ocala, FL | Urethane Enamel
description: Cabinet refinishing in Ocala, FL: degreased, sanded, primed, and finished in waterborne urethane enamel. A new-looking kitchen without tearing out boxes.
h1: Cabinet Refinishing in Ocala, FL for Kitchens Worth Keeping
heroIntro: If your Ocala kitchen's layout works and the cabinet boxes are sound, refinishing changes the look without demolition. We degrease, sand, prime, and enamel every surface.

sections.h2: Ocala kitchens that are good refinishing candidates
body: Many Ocala homes have cabinets that are structurally fine but visually tired. In mid-century houses around neighborhoods like Magnolia, that often means solid wood boxes under an old finish. In newer homes in places like Bellechase or Marion Oaks, it is often builder-grade cabinetry in a color the owner never chose. In both cases, cabinet refinishing in Ocala, FL keeps the layout and boxes and replaces only the finish.

Refinishing is not right for every kitchen. Swollen particleboard, failing hinges, or a layout you want to change all point toward replacement. Our article on refinishing versus replacing cabinets lays out how to decide.

Kitchen grease is the enemy of adhesion, so prep is most of the job. Every door, drawer front, and face frame is cleaned with a degreaser, scuff-sanded, and primed with a bonding primer before color. The topcoat is waterborne urethane enamel, which cures hard enough for daily hands, pots, and cleaning sprays and stays low in odor while you live in the house.

Sheen is part of the decision. Satin is the most forgiving choice for busy family kitchens, while semi-gloss is easier to wipe but shows every dent in older doors. We brush out samples so you can compare them on your own cabinet faces before we commit to a full run.
bullets: Doors, drawers, and hardware removed and labelled
Degrease, scuff-sand, and fill as needed
Bonding primer, then two coats of urethane enamel
Counters, floors, and appliances masked and protected
Hardware reinstalled and doors adjusted at the end

sections.h2: Oak grain and other honest expectations
body: Oak has open grain that will show through paint unless it is filled. We discuss that choice at the walkthrough, because some owners like the texture and others want a smooth, modern look. Our guide to painting oak cabinets shows both outcomes. Color matching works from a chip, a sample door, or a leftover can, and you see full-size drawdowns before we commit.

sections.h2: How long your Ocala kitchen is out of service
body: Timing depends on door count, repairs, and whether grain filling is included, and the written estimate lists the schedule before we start. The kitchen stays partially usable, and we protect counters and appliances each day. Many owners pair the job with a fresh coat on the surrounding walls through our interior painting in Ocala. Read more about our cabinet painting and refinishing service, or head back to the Ocala location page.

faqs.q: Do you paint bathroom vanities as well as kitchen cabinets?
faqs.a: Yes. Vanities, built-ins, and laundry cabinets get the same degrease, prime, and urethane enamel system and can be added to the kitchen estimate.

faqs.q: Can I still use my Ocala kitchen during cabinet refinishing?
faqs.a: Partially. We protect counters and appliances and keep the work organized so the kitchen stays usable for basics while doors and boxes are being finished.

faqs.q: What if a door chips after the job is done?
faqs.a: We leave labelled touch-up paint in your cabinet color so small chips can be blended in later.

faqs.q: Do you also paint the kitchen island or a built-in bar?
faqs.a: Yes. Islands, pantry doors, bar cabinets, and other built-ins can be added to the same estimate and finished in the same urethane enamel so everything matches.
